And you? What does a normal day look like for you?

My sister and I live in the same building, and our days could not be more different. She wakes up at five. Five. Nobody asks her to; she just does. She runs for forty minutes, she takes a cold shower, and by seven she has already answered every message she owes anybody. She never leaves the house without breakfast. I usually leave without my shoes on properly. She works from an office and she goes to about six meetings a day, and she says she likes them, which I do not understand at all. She does not check her phone after nine at night. She does not watch television. She reads. On Saturday she cleans the whole apartment before I am even awake, and then she asks me what I did all week. My routine is simpler. I wake up late, I work from home, I forget lunch, and I go to bed at two in the morning. We get on very well. We just never see each other before noon.

People think a routine makes your life smaller. In my experience it does the opposite. A routine is a set of decisions you make once, so that you do not have to make them again every morning while you are still half asleep. My neighbor gets up at the same time every single day, including Sunday. She walks her dog on the same street, she buys bread at the same place, and the man there starts making her coffee when he sees her cross the road. It sounds boring. It is not. Everything else in her week is chaos, and those forty minutes are the part nobody can move. So look at your own week and find the part that never changes. If there is nothing, that is the problem. Not the meetings, not the hours, not the traffic. The problem is that there is no hour in your week that belongs to you and always happens.
